I’ll review the committed branch changes and all staged, unstaged, and untracked work, then trace affected callers and contracts. I’ll keep the review read-only and report actionable findings with file references.

This is a large ownership refactor spanning UI, shared state, runtime, persistence, extensions, and test infrastructure. My review checklist is: map moves and substantive changes, trace lifecycle and data behavior, run relevant checks, then verify each finding against the original code.

content.text:
Found **two actionable issues** in the staged, unstaged, and untracked changes.

1. **[P1] Workspace renames break frontend deployments.**  
   [apps/nucleus/package.json:2](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/apps/nucleus/package.json:2) renames the workspace to `@nucleum/app`; Memotron and Pointron are also renamed. However, [deployment configuration](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/services/frontend/config/environments.json:25) still contains `nucleus-app`, `memotron-app`, and `pointron-app`. The [deployment script](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/services/frontend/scripts/deploy.mjs:36) passes these directly to npm, so normal deployments fail before building. Confirmed with `npm --workspace nucleus-app run`, which returns `No workspaces found`. Update all three deployment selectors with the package renames.

2. **[P2] Incomplete caller migration leaves architecture and unit-test gates failing.**  
   Several tests still reference removed modules or exports:
   - [resource-action-host.test.ts:32](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/resources/resource-action-host.test.ts:32) imports the relocated `resource.actions` and `bulk-editor` modules from their old locations, preventing the suite from loading.
   - [nucleus.datafn.test.ts:8](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/products/nucleus/nucleus.datafn.test.ts:8) imports `resolveDatafnBootResources` from `datafn.store`, although it now belongs to `resource-selection`.
   - [import-legacy-data.test.ts:16](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/persistence/migrations/import-legacy-data.test.ts:16) and [legacy-data-recovery.test.ts:43](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/settings/data-recovery/legacy-data-recovery.test.ts:43) mock the deleted `legacyLocalDataBackup` module. The mocks no longer intercept the extracted implementations, causing eight failures.

   Update these callers and mock targets to the new owners. The current state produces **five architecture violations, nine failed tests, and one unloadable suite**.

Verification covered the ownership changes, substantive logic changes, host wiring, lifecycle extraction, extension entry points, and deployment callers:

- **Passed:** all four product compiler checks; type ownership; retired-runtime checks; fixed-wait checks; diff whitespace checks.
- **Unit tests:** 103 files passed, four failed; 391 tests passed, nine failed.
- **Not exercised:** browser/Playwright workflows, native packaging, production builds, or deployment.

No source files or index entries were changed.
